analysis:
Examined the head text of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (lines 552-1671) and the StartupPreload patch. The security-relevant changes are memory-admission and eviction logic: reclaimableMemoryBytes now optionally counts CBv2RetainedKVSegments.retainedBytes; new evictionCanReach helper; evictUntilAvailable and fastAdmissionReject release retained KV segments and clear the MLX cache before resampling; StartupPreload adds a reclaimBeforeSkip hook that calls releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad. No finding was identified. This is internal capacity accounting with no new external input, no change to authentication or attestation, and no change to the coordinator wire contract or plaintext handling.

The model-load path in the first unit (lines 552-1046) is shown as context. Its TOCTOU bracketing of weight hashes (lines 597-641) and the artifactIdentityRequired / cacheEligibleWeightHash flow into ModelSlot are unchanged in the visible patch ranges. They relate to T-041 (SSD cache bound to verified weightHash) and T-012/T-027, and I saw no weakening of them. The changed ranges begin at line 1305, so the earlier hashing logic is unchanged.

The release of retained KV segments and clearCache touches only free segments and buffer pools. This relates to T-028 (residual GPU data): clearing more memory is neutral to beneficial. It does not affect the SSD cache's at-rest posture, TTL, HMAC names, or salt scoping.

Availability considerations (T-029, T-010): the extra release calls could add latency or churn, because fastAdmissionReject is on the pre-accept path and now calls releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad, which can wait briefly and drop retained segments for engines. This is a mutation in a path documented as non-mutating, but it only drops reclaimable pools and falls back to recompute. I did not see unbounded impact, but a consumer who can send requests for unloadable models might repeatedly trigger the release and degrade throughput of other models. This is speculative; the visible code does not show the rate limiting in the coordinator.

Remaining unverified: the implementations of CBv2RetainedKVSegments, GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments and the StartupPreloader consumer of reclaimBeforeSkip are outside the supplied evidence.
